about: CANOPY write outcomes, one entry per row id. `source` names who decides the outcome: `connector` (the PV connector behind Hare, answering the PUT), `front` (canopy_mcp, before anything is sent upstream) or `client` (the viewer, with no response to go on). `detail` is the envelope detail and equals the toast for every server row; `<...>` marks the dynamic part (connector-refused and connector-limits: the connector's message, mismatch: the observed value, write-state-changed: the heartbeat frame's `label`). A detail longer than `detail_max_chars` is cut at the last whitespace before that limit with … appended, so it never ends inside a word. `detail_cut_cases` are the cases that define that cut: `text` cut to `limit` characters is `expected`, a character being one Unicode code point. `default` is the detail used when a dynamic row has no message (write-state-changed: a null label). connector-refused-read-only is connector-refused when the whole deployment runs read-only. `status`/`code` null: no response or no envelope. coalesced: `outcome` is the winner's, no toast for the superseded value; `toast` is the viewer's text for a run stopped by it.
